h1.cap: Name the five people you talk to most. That list... is your real CV.

n2.cap: Siena... over 500 years ago. Its lord, Pandolfo Petrucci, had a right-hand man.

n3.cap: Antonio da Venafro. People judged Pandolfo... by him.

n4.cap: In essence, Machiavelli says Pandolfo looked clever... simply for having him.

q1.cap: His words... "the first opinion which one forms of a prince... is by observing the men he has around him."

n5.cap: Then he sorts minds into three kinds.

n6.cap: One works things out alone. One recognises good ideas from others. One does neither.

q2.cap: His verdict... "the first is the most excellent, the second is good, the third is useless."

n7.cap: So you don't need to be the genius. Spotting good minds... is a power of its own.

n8.cap: Group project. Pick the quiet kid who reads the brief... and you look brilliant on results day.

n9.cap: Now flip it. You're in someone's circle too. Make them look wise.

n10.cap: This morning, message one person who makes you sharper... and tell them why.

n11.cap: Who's the Venafro in your corner? Tell us what they do for you.

n12.cap: Choose your circle well... and follow Awazzzz.
